summary:
Región de Valparaíso stands under the national framework of Chile: the legal regime, document rules, entry provisions and protection machinery are those set out in the national record. What is specific to the region is the distribution of recorded anti-LGBTI discrimination cases and a municipal diversity-office structure.

Movilh's XXIV annual human rights report, published in March 2026 and covering 2025, records that Valparaíso concentrated 51.32% of the anti-LGBTI discrimination cases recorded nationally in 2024, an increase of 80.93% on 2023. That is a share of recorded cases, not a per-capita rate, and no population denominator accompanies it; recorded cases reflect where monitoring organisations operate and where victims report, as well as where incidents occur.

In 2025 recorded cases fell in Valparaíso and in the Región Metropolitana while every other region rose. Movilh reads the pattern as hostility moving toward regions where LGBTIQ issues have less visibility.
tangentialFactors:
Valparaíso and the Región Metropolitana were the only two regions where recorded anti-LGBTI discrimination cases fell in 2025; every other region recorded a rise. The same national legal framework applies in all of them, so the divergence reflects reporting and local conditions rather than differences in statute.

The municipal diversity-office model is not confined to Valparaíso. The first Encuentro de Oficinas Municipales de Diversidad was held in Valparaíso in 2022, the second in Melipilla in 2023 and the third in Concepción in 2024.
localsOnly:
Valparaíso hosted the first Encuentro de Oficinas Municipales de Diversidad in 2022. San Antonio was among the founding comunas of the Red de Municipalidades por la Diversidad, Inclusión y No Discriminación (Red Diversa), created in 2014 as a network of municipalities with LGBTIQA+ offices or programmes; by 2024 it had grown beyond 60 municipalities.

For residents, those municipal offices and programmes are the local points of contact for discrimination complaints and support. The region holds the largest share of nationally recorded anti-LGBTI discrimination cases, 51.32% in 2024, and its recorded cases fell in 2025.
outOfScopeNotes:
The 51.32% share is of recorded cases, not a per-capita rate, and no population denominator for Región de Valparaíso appears in the sources. It cannot establish that a visitor or resident in Valparaíso faces a higher per-person risk than elsewhere in Chile; recorded cases also depend on the presence of monitoring organisations and on victims' willingness to report.

Whether the 2025 fall in recorded cases in Valparaíso reflects fewer incidents or reduced reporting is not resolved by the source.

No region-specific trans homicide or violence figures for Región de Valparaíso appear in the sources; the emblematic cases and the national anti-violence record are carried by the national record.

The Movilh series runs per region and per commune from 2002 to 2025; only the 2024 and 2025 figures appear in the sources.
